quote: Some of the most devastating fungal pathogens in wheat are leaf rust, stripe rust, and powdery mildew. The wheat gene Lr34 has supported resistance to these pathogens for more than 50 years.
notes: resistance_type=APR is supported by a later sentence in the same abstract ('functions in the adult plant'), not by the quoted span itself -- ground.py only requires the subject/object surface text inside the quote, not every qualifier value.

quote: The wheat gene Sr33, introgressed from the wild relative Aegilops tauschii into bread wheat, confers resistance to diverse stem rust races, including the Ug99 race group.
notes: resistance_type left as 'unknown' on purpose: this abstract (the only text Europe PMC serves for this non-open-access paper, so the only text extract_paper itself can see) never states seedling/all-stage vs adult-plant timing. kg/curated/wheat_seed_genes.yaml records Sr33 elsewhere as an all-stage NLR gene, but that comes from outside this abstract -- annotating 'unknown' here matches what the pipeline can actually see, not outside knowledge, per docs/annotation_guidelines.md Sec 3.

quote: We report the map-based cloning of the leaf rust resistance gene Lr21, previously mapped to a gene-rich region at the distal end of chromosome arm 1DS of bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.).
notes: Direct, single-sentence resistance statement (unlike Lr34/Rcs3's indirect backreference pattern) -- included specifically to test whether the pipeline handles the straightforward case reliably. resistance_type left 'unknown': the abstract never states seedling/all-stage vs adult-plant timing.

quote: Fhb1 is the most consistently reported quantitative trait locus (QTL) for FHB resistance breeding.
notes: object_text is the abbreviation 'FHB' exactly as it appears in this quote; object_id is the correct canonical entity (dis:wheat:fusarium_head_blight) even though config/vocab/diseases.yaml's synonym list for this disease is only ['head scab'] -- 'FHB' is NOT registered as a synonym. Deliberately tests whether the live resolver can handle this common abbreviation; a 'could not resolve object' rejection here would be a real synonym-vocabulary gap, not a hallucination.

quote: The most advantageous conditions for the progress of powdery mildew on wheat were low temperature and ambient CO2.
notes: This is the paper's own primary finding (real full-text paper, not an abstract-only pilot). object_id is null on purpose: DISEASE_ENV_TRIGGER's object is always a brand-new EnvTrigger entity that build_claim_candidate deliberately routes to a human curator (curator/extract/normalize.py's NEW_ENTITY_TYPES) -- expect this to land in the harness's gold_needs_human_entity bucket, not count as a miss, exactly as documented in docs/annotation_guidelines.md Sec 2. A more specific numeric version of this same finding exists in the Discussion ('Low temperatures (18-22C) and ambient CO2 (450 ppm)...') but that sentence never names the disease by name -- it says only 'disease development'/'the pathogen' -- the disease name is only in an earlier sentence 3 sentences back. Deliberately chose the cleaner, self-contained abstract sentence for this gold record instead of stacking a 3-sentence cross-reference on top of everything else being tested.

quote: Powdery mildew caused by Blumeria (syn. Erysiphe) graminis (DC) E.O. Speer f. sp. tritici Em. Marchal (Bgt) is one of the most important foliar disease on wheat worldwide, particularly in humid areas with a semi-continental or maritime climate (Bennett, 1984; Cowger et al., 2012).
notes: object_text is the paper's own abbreviation 'Bgt', used throughout the rest of the paper -- object_id is the correct canonical entity (path:blumeria_graminis_f_sp_tritici) even though config/vocab/diseases.yaml has NO pathogen_synonyms entry at all for this pathogen (unlike Cercospora sojina, fixed earlier this session). The full taxonomic name in this sentence ('Blumeria (syn. Erysiphe) graminis (DC) E.O. Speer f. sp. tritici Em. Marchal') is not even a contiguous substring of the canonical vocab name (the parenthetical synonym insertion breaks it up), so a naive full-name extraction couldn't resolve either -- this deliberately tests whether the live resolver can handle a common in-paper abbreviation for a pathogen with zero registered synonyms.
